semantics: the game's resolved HDRP colour grading at rip time, read from VolumeManager's post-blend volume stack. CS2's ground albedo is authored near-grey and this is what turns it into the on-screen palette. Optional: a consumer that wants the raw albedo should ignore this block entirely; one that wants the game's look should apply it as a display transform, NOT bake it into the shipped textures
order: exposure -> white balance -> color adjustments (filter, contrast, hue, saturation) -> shadows/midtones/highlights -> tonemapping
note: a snapshot of one moment: grading follows weather and time of day, so a rip taken at dusk records dusk

colorAdjustments.units: postExposure in EV/stops; the rest on HDRP's -100..100

shadowsMidtonesHighlights.units: each is [r, g, b, w]: rgb a per-channel multiplier around 1.0, w an offset

tonemapping.note: the display transform the grading above was authored against

lighting.semantics: the illumination the grading above sits on top of. A consumer that reproduces the albedo and the grading but lights the scene white will still miss the game's colour: the sun is not white

sun.units: `color` is the light's own filter as authored
sun.directionUnits: `direction` is the unit vector the light TRAVELS along

sky.units: HDRP PhysicallyBasedSky; this is the ambient half of the light

time.units: in-game clock and map position at rip time
